jobs.description:
Overview:

GovCIO is currently hiring for a Program Manager to own the day-to-day delivery of a large federal health IT program and serve as a primary client-facing point of contact. This position will be fully remote within the United States, with some meeting-related travel.

Responsibilities:

Directs all phases of programs from inception through completion. Responsible for the schedule and performance of company programs or subsystems of major programs. Acts as primary customer contact for program activities, leading program review sessions with the customer to discuss, schedule, and technical performance. Establishes milestones and monitors adherence to master plans and schedules, identifies program problems and obtains solutions, such as allocation of resources. Directs the work of employees assigned to the program.The program is governed through an Integrated Product Team model with regular steering-level oversight, and delivery runs on a two-week sprint cadence inside a weekly client-workstream  
rhythm. The right candidate is comfortable holding the client relationship, running a structured  
operating model, and surfacing risk early and plainly

* Manages one or more programs of size and complexity, may manage an operating/field office, and supervises professional and technical personnel performing in their customary disciplines.
* Maintains aggressive efforts to achieve objectives.
* Prepares manpower staffing plans, including skill and labor mix, to support contract operations. May be responsible for recruiting, interviewing, and hiring staff.
* Monitors contract compliance and deliverables.
* Acquires follow-on business associated with areas of responsibility and supports new business development.
* Translate client priorities into delivery direction and represent delivery status, risks, and decisions to the client clearly and credibly.
* Maintain the dependency map across the seven workstreams and keep entangled workstreams synchronized, so issues are worked before they cascade.
* Work with the managers to balance staff across workstreams, watching for concentration risk where individuals carry multiple workstreams or where a workstream has thin backup coverage.
* Maintain the program risk register, surface strategic risks explicitly and early, and own mitigation tracking.
* Ensure delivery artifacts are accurate, internally consistent, and traceable across documents — a recurring need in a multi-workstream program.

Qualifications:

**Required Skills and Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree and 15+ years of experience. (or commensurate experience)
  + 7+ years of program or project management experience, including  
    direct management of staff.
* Demonstrated experience as a primary client-facing point of contact on a complex  
  program, owning the relationship day to day.
* Experience running a structured delivery operating model across multiple concurrent  
  workstreams, with hands-on dependency, risk, and action management.
* Working knowledge of Agile / SAFe delivery, including sprint planning, PI planning, and  
  cadence-based coordination

**Clearance Required:** Ability to obtain and maintain a Suitability/Public Trust clearance.

**Preferred Skills and Experience:**

* Experience in federal health IT, VA / VHA programs, or other regulated government health  
  environments.
* PMP, SAFe (e.g., SAFe Agilist / RTE), or equivalent certification.
* Experience supporting clinical or EHR-adjacent technology rollouts at enterprise scale.

jobs.description:
This position provides critical Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM) and Vendor Threat Mitigation (VTM) planning, coordination, and intelligence-integration. The role ensures the security and resilience of the theater supply chain by identifying, assessing, and mitigating vendor-related risks?including foreign ownership, control, or influence (FOCI), cyber vulnerabilities, and adversarial exploitation?across the Area of Responsibility (AOR). The role is highly dynamic and adaptive to command priorities; requiring an experienced professional who can operate independently with minimal guidance.
  
  
The VTM Program Analyst serves as a key contractor supporting Geographic Combatant Command (GCC) secure logistics objectives. The role focuses on the strategic planning of vendor threat assessments and supply chain illumination, aligned with the Theater Campaign Plan, Posture Plan, and Department of Defense (DoD) SCRM directives. A primary requirement is the ability to conduct high-level risk framework analysis and all-source intelligence reports, integrate them for mitigation actions into major joint operations, exercise support, and coalition logistics. As required, forward adversarial findings and reports to respective procurement contracting agencies and associated authorities to take direct action against vendor threats. Exceptional written and oral communication skills, with the ability to successfully collaborate in multi-echelon Joint Logistics and Intelligence Enterprises (JLEnt/JIE), are mandatory for success in this role.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities:**  
**Threat Analysis & Illumination:** Conduct rigorous supply chain illuminations and vendor threat assessments to identify FOCI, cyber vulnerabilities, and adversarial influence risks within the AOR, ensuring mission requirements are protected from compromised suppliers.
  
  
**Mitigation Planning:** Develop and implement theater-specific VTM mitigation strategies and risk response plans, ensuring alignment with DoD security protocols and mission-critical function protection.
  
  
**Exercise & Operation Integration:** Support VTM planning for Tier 1 and Tier 2 Exercises (e.g., Balikatan, Cobra Gold), ensuring theater supply chains are modeled, stress-tested against subversion, and assessed during major training events.
  
  
**Interagency & Partner Sync:** Synchronize vendor threat intelligence and mitigation strategies with USFK, USFJ, SOCPAC, and regional Service Components. Coordinate with DCSA, DLA, and USTRANSCOM to ensure a unified theater defense.
  
  
**Governance & Reporting:** Serve as a subject matter expert for VTM policy and governance. Draft formal staff products (EXSUMs, Info Papers) and deliver executive-level briefings to General/Flag Officers (GO/FO) regarding theater supply chain vulnerabilities.
  
  
The candidate must demonstrate a deep understanding of and the ability to apply the following Joint Publications (JPs), DoD Directives and Instructions (DoDD/DoDI), and associated policies that support theater distribution security and vendor threat mitigation:
  
**? DoDD 5000.01, The Defense Acquisition System:** Mandates supply chain risk management, security, and resilience throughout the acquisition lifecycle and sustainment operations.
  
**? DoDD 5240.02, Counterintelligence (CI):** Establishes foundational CI policy essential for identifying and mitigating foreign intelligence threats, FOCI, and espionage within the vendor base.
  
**? DoDI 5200.44:** Protection of Mission Critical Functions to Achieve Trusted Systems and Networks (TSN).
  
**? DoDI 4140.01:** DoD Supply Chain Materiel Management Policy (with focus on SCRM and resilience).
  
**? DoDI 5000.90:** Cybersecurity for Acquisition Decision Authorities and Program Managers.
  
**? JP 4-0 / JP 4-01:** Joint Logistics and the Joint Deployment and Distribution Enterprise (JDDE).
  
**? JP 4-10, Operational Contract Support (OCS):** Integration of commercial support into joint operations, including the assessment of vendor-related risks to force protection and mission assurance.
  
**? JP 2-0 / JP 3-0:** Joint Intelligence and Joint Operations integration for threat-informed logistics.
  
**? NDAA Compliance:** Specific expertise in Sections 889 (telecommunications) and 5949 (semiconductors) prohibitions within theater of operations.
